newsitem.title: UK: Esprit Telecom plans submarine cable links.
newsitem.headline: Esprit Telecom plans submarine cable links.

text.p: Newly-floated Esprit Telecom Group Plc said on Monday it was seeking to expand its network by building two submarine cable systems linking the U.K., the Netherlands and France.

The Amsterdam-headquartered company, that raised about $50 million by completing an initial public flotation in the U.S. earlier this month, said the high capacity links would be capable of transmitting 180,000 simultaneous telephone calls.
The European telecoms firm has sent proposal requests to cable laying companies to evaluate the cost and potential savings of building such links under the Channel and North Sea.
If the terms offered by cable companies are not deemed competitive enough, a spokeswoman said Esprit was also looking at several other options of expanding its network bandwidth cost-effectively.

Free to build its own network since winning an international facilities licence in the UK last year, Esprit Telecom expects submarine cables to yield 'important cost savings' so it can maintain competitive services to business and telecoms carrier customers.
The company said it would fund a new cable system through pre-selling part of its capacity to other carriers, finance leasing and existing resources.

Esprit Telecom's network links 14 cities in the UK, the Netherlands, Spain, France, Germany, Belgium, Italy and Ireland and offers customised international and national long distance telecoms services to large and medium-sized businesses.

The UK government has granted international licences to more than 44 operators, so that these no longer need to pay high fees to dominant carriers British Telecommunications Plc or Cable and Wireless Plc to carry international traffic to and from the UK.
